name: Scenario
summary: Builds consistent game art pipelines with custom style models and batch generation.
detail: Scenario provides hosted image, video, 3D and audio workflows, custom-model training, a REST API and an official beta MCP interface. Inspect each model schema before submission; MCP model_run can return an unfinished job rather than output assets. The documented job_cancel cannot cancel jobs created by model_run or workflow_run. Integration examples do not include the full hosted service or a complete game project.

tutorial.note: Official walkthrough for custom style training, batch generation, and asset delivery.

name: Meshy API
summary: Connects AI model generation, humanoid rigging, and animation export for game asset workflows.
detail: The official animated-character recipe turns a reference image into a textured, rigged character with idle, jump, and attack clips in GLB and FBX. The animation step applies motions from Meshy's library. API rigging works best with standard textured bipeds with clearly separated limbs. Generated assets still need engine import, collision, controls, and performance checks; the public cookbook supplies asset examples rather than complete gameplay.

tutorial.label: Image to animated character
tutorial.note: Official guide with reference files, Python and TypeScript examples, and GLB/FBX outputs. API access uses credits.

demo.note: Hosted generation and animation workspace; account access is required to generate assets. This is not a playable game.

source.note: Public asset-generation recipes, not Meshy's model source or a complete game project.

name: HY-Motion 1.0
summary: Generates skeletal humanoid motion from text with public inference code and model weights.
detail: Tencent's text-to-motion models produce human character animation, with CLI inference, local Gradio visualization, and a hosted model demo. Use the generated motion as an animation-pipeline input and retarget it to the target character. The documented limitations include non-humanoid motion, multi-person interaction, seamless loops, and in-place animation. The release provides a motion implementation, not a controllable game character or full game project. Its custom license excludes the EU, UK and South Korea and restricts using the works or outputs to improve other AI models, except HY-Motion and its derivatives. Review the exact license and commercial threshold before adoption.

tutorial.label: Installation and motion workflow
tutorial.note: Official setup, CLI inference, local UI, and prompting guidance. Local execution requires the documented GPU resources.

demo.note: Official text-to-motion model interface; a motion preview rather than playable gameplay. Hosted availability may vary.

source.note: Public inference and visualization implementation with separately linked weights; no complete game project.

name: ElevenLabs Sound Effects
summary: Generates game sound effects, Foley, and looping ambience from text through a web app or API.
detail: Describe footsteps, impacts, UI feedback, or environmental sounds, control duration, and export audio for a game engine. The documentation describes loop-enabled generation for seamless repeat playback and a 30-second maximum per clip. Its overview lists MP3 for all effects and 48 kHz WAV for non-looping effects; API format support and plan requirements should be checked separately. Loop quality still needs validation in the target game. This is a hosted audio service. The public SDK connects to its API and does not release the generation model or a complete game project.

tutorial.label: Sound Effects quickstart
tutorial.note: Official API walkthrough with SDK examples; an account and API key are needed for generation.

demo.label: Sound effects generator
demo.note: Official text-to-audio generator and sound examples; this is an audio tool, not a playable game.

source.note: API client source only; generation model and complete game source are not included.

name: Stable Audio Open 1.0
summary: Provides downloadable text-to-audio weights and local tools for sound effects and field recordings.
detail: Generates up to 47 seconds of stereo audio at 44.1 kHz, with examples for local inference and WAV export. The official audio-tools repository includes a local Gradio interface. The model works best with English descriptions, is stronger at sound effects and field recordings than music, and cannot produce realistic vocals. Model access requires accepting its terms and sharing contact information with the publisher; this resource is an audio pipeline rather than a complete soundtrack or game generator.

tutorial.note: Official model usage examples for stable-audio-tools and Diffusers.
